paper.title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Regret for Linearly Parameterized Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Linear contextual bandit with finite action sets (upper bound)
unmapped: at most n_act candidate actions per round; algorithm uses n_act
action sets chosen obliviously by an adversary before execution
settings.definition_quote: At each time period $t$, a \emph{policy} $\pi$ is presented with an \emph{action set} $\mathcal A_t=\{x_{it}\}\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb R^d: \|x\|_2\leq 1\}$ ... receives a reward $r_t=x_{it}^\top\theta + \eps_t$, where $\{\eps_t\}$ are independent centered sub-Gaussian random variables with variance proxy $1$

unmapped: at most n_act actions per round, learner knows n_act

unmapped: closed infinite action sets inside the unit ball that change over time
settings.definition_quote: there exists a bandit instance with regression model $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$, $\|\theta\|_2\leq 1$ and closed action spaces $\mathcal A_1,\cdots,\mathcal A_T\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\|x\|_2\leq 1\}$, $|\mathcal A_t|=\infty$

symbols.n_act: maximum number of actions per round (paper's n)
symbols.gamma_pl: unspecified positive constant exponent of the poly(log log(nT)) factor

source.label: thm:upper-finite
source.quote: For any $n<\infty$, the minimax regret $\mathfrak R(T;n,d)$ can be asymptotically upper bounded by $\mathrm{poly}(\log\log(nT))\cdot O(\sqrt{dT(\log T)(\log n)})$.

results.notes: Stated as bound on minimax regret, achieved by VCL-SupLinUCB (Sec. 2). Regret defined via means, so pseudo-regret. Remark 3: poly(loglog(nT)) = (loglog(nT))^gamma.

symbols.n_act: maximum number of actions per round (paper's n)
symbols.eps_alg: small constant epsilon > 0 in the condition on T

conditions: T >= d*(log_2 n_act)^(1+eps_alg) for some constant eps_alg > 0

source.label: thm:lower-finite
source.quote: For any small constant $\epsilon > 0$, and any $n,d, $ such that $n \leq 2^{d/2}$ and $T \geq d (\log_2 n)^{1+\epsilon}$, the minimax regret $\mathfrak R(T;n,d)$ can be asymptotically lower bounded by $\Omega(1)\cdot\sqrt{dT(\log n)\log (T/d)}$.

symbols.n_act: maximum number of actions per round (paper's n)

source.label: thm:LB-n-eq-expd
source.quote: Suppose $T\geq d^5$ and $n=2^{d/2}$. Then $\mathfrak R(T;n,d) = \Omega(1)\cdot d\sqrt{T\log T}$.

results.notes: Gaussian noise variance 1 in hard instances.

bound.regime: T >= d^(2+eps_alg), n_act = 2^(d/2), d sufficiently large

symbols.n_act: maximum number of actions per round (paper's n)
symbols.eps_alg: small constant epsilon > 0 in the condition T >= d^(2+epsilon)

source.label: thm:lb-n-eq-expd-strengthened
source.quote: For any small constant $\epsilon > 0$ and sufficiently large $d$, suppose $T\geq d^{2+\eps}$ and $n=2^{d/2}$. Then $\mathfrak R(T;n,d) = \Omega(1)\cdot d\sqrt{\epsilon T\log T}$.

conditions: action sets infinite, closed, and changing over time

source.label: cor:infinite-action
source.quote: For any policy $\pi$, there exists a bandit instance with regression model $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$, $\|\theta\|_2\leq 1$ and closed action spaces $\mathcal A_1,\cdots,\mathcal A_T\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\|x\|_2\leq 1\}$, $|\mathcal A_t|=\infty$, such that for sufficiently large $T$, $\mathbb E[R^T] = \Omega(d\sqrt{T\log T})$.

results.notes: Derived by reduction from Theorems 10/21; implicit relation between T and d (T >= d^(2+eps)) inherited.
